verse.text: bhavadbhaktyamṛtāsvādād bodhasya syāt parāpi yā / daśā sā māṃ prati svāmin nāsavasyeva śuktatā

howto.text: When longing is loud: say the verse and let the object of the longing become the taste of devotion rather than the thing you'd grab.

verse.text: kṣaṇam apīha na tāvakadāsatāṃ prati bhaveyam ahaṃ kila bhājanam / bhavadabhedarasāsavam ādarād avirataṃ rasayeyam ahaṃ na cet

howto.text: When you crave closeness to something: say it and re-cast — the wine is already poured (non-difference); you are the cup.

verse.text: ambudaiḥ śikhigaṇo vinādyate kā ratiḥ priya mayā vinādya te

howto.text: When longing for someone or something: say it as the peacock line — the cry is appropriate, beautiful, and will end with the rain. Feel the ache as weather: you are the bird, not the drowning.

verse.text: prakāśāṃ śītalām ekāṃ śuddhāṃ śaśikalām iva / dṛśaṃ vitara me nātha kām apy amṛtavāhinīm

howto.text: When desire runs hot: one breath in, offer the heat upward as the thing that needs the glance, and picture the crescent-cool gaze landing on it. The prayer cools by image, not by prohibition.

verse.text: hasyate nṛtyate yatra rāgadveṣādi bhujyate / pīyate bhaktipīyūṣarasas tat prāpnuyāṃ padam

howto.text: Say it when something finally stops being infuriating — and notice the laugh that arrives is the verse working.

verse.text: upahāsaikasāre 'sminn etāvati jagattraye / tubhyam evādvitīyāya namo nityasukhāsine

howto.text: When life turns absurd: say it, and read the absurdity as his seat.

verse.text: jayanti te jagadvandyā dāsās te jagatāṃ vibho / saṃsārārṇava evaiṣa yeṣāṃ krīḍāmahāsaraḥ

howto.text: In a hard moment, name it: ocean. Then say the verse, and the water becomes shallow.

verse.text: bhaktikṣīvo 'pi kupyeyaṃ bhavāyānuśayīya ca / tathā haseyaṃ udyāṃ ca raṭeyaṃ ca śivety alam

howto.text: When worked up: say it as an instruction manual — drunk first, then let it become laugh, rise, and shout. The last word must be Śiva, out loud if you dare.

verse.text: citraṃ nisargato nātha duḥkhabījam idaṃ manaḥ / tvadbhaktirasasaṃsiktam niḥśreyasamahāphalam

howto.text: In grief: say it and water the seed instead of cursing the soil.

verse.text: harṣāṇām atha śokānāṃ sarveṣāṃ plāvakaḥ samam / bhavaddhyānāmṛtāpūro nimnāṇimnabhuvām iva

howto.text: Say it in either state — grief or glee — the verse works on the level of the field, not the feeling.

verse.text: deva duḥkhāny aśeṣāṇi yāni saṃsāriṇām api / ghṛtyākhyabhavadīyātmayutāny āyānti sahyatām

howto.text: In pain: say the ghee line and literally imagine the sharp edge of the feeling being coated.

verse.text: he nātha praṇatārtināśanapaṭo śreyonidhe dhūrjaṭe duḥkhaikāyatanasya janmamaraṇatrastasya me sāmpratam / tac ceṣṭasva yathā manojñaviṣayāsvādapradā uttamā jīvann eva samaśnuve 'ham acalāḥ siddhīs tvadarcāparaḥ

howto.text: At 3am in the pit: say the whole confession first, then the name.

verse.text: etan mama na tv idam iti rāgadveṣādinigaḍadṛḍhamūle / nātha bhavanmayataikyapratyayaparaśuḥ patatvantaḥ

howto.text: In rage: name the possession first — 'mine', 'not yours' — then say the verse at it.

verse.text: mānāvamānarāgādiniṣpākavimalaṃ manaḥ / yasyāsau bhaktimāṃl lokatulyaśīlaḥ kathaṃ bhavet

howto.text: When slighted: say it and let the feeling ripen rather than react — the insult is being cooked, not served.

verse.text: rāgadveṣandhakāro 'pi yeṣāṃ bhaktitviṣā jitaḥ / teṣāṃ mahīyasām agre katame jñānaśālinaḥ

howto.text: Say it as a light-switch claim: the anger is dark, and you are switching on devotion rather than wrestling the dark.

verse.text: vandyās te 'pi mahīyāṃsaḥ pralayopagatā api / tvatkopapāvakasparśapūtā ye parameśvara

howto.text: When caught in a rage — yours or someone's's: say it, and re-classify the fire as purifying touch before responding.

verse.text: jaya deva namo namo 'stu te sakalaṃ viśvam idaṃ tavāśritam / jagatāṃ parameśvaro bhavān paramekaḥ śaraṇāgato 'smi te

howto.text: Morning, before the task: say it once under the breath, fast.

verse.text: antarbhakticamatkāracarvaṇāmīlitekṣaṇaḥ / namo mahyaṃ śivāyeti pūjayam syāṃ tṛṇāny api

howto.text: When enthusiasm needs depth rather than noise: say it and offer to be the least impressive thing in the room.

verse.text: te jayanti mukhamaṇḍale bhraman asti yeṣu niyataṃ śivadhvaniḥ / yaḥ śāśīva prasṛto 'mṛtāśayāt svādu saṃsravati cāmṛtaṃ param

howto.text: Say it when you catch the name rising on its own — mid-shower, mid-walk. The verse applauds the practice applauding itself.

verse.text: capalam asi yad api mānasa tatrāpi ślāghyase yato bhajase / śaraṇānām api śaraṇaṃ tribhuvanagurum ambikākāntam

howto.text: Address it TO your mind, in the second person, when it won't hold — praise it for showing up rather than scolding it for drifting.

verse.text: īśvaram abhayam udāraṃ pūrṇam akāraṇam apahnutātmānaṃ / sahasābhijñāya kadā svāmijanaṃ lajjayiṣyāmi

howto.text: When fear is up: say it as a question, not a plea — kadā? when?.

verse.text: mūḍho 'smi duḥkhakalito 'smi jarādidoṣabhīto 'smi śaktirahito 'smi tavāśrito 'smi / śambho tathā kalaya śīghram upaimi yena sarvottamāṃ dhuram apojjhitaduḥkhamārgaḥ

howto.text: List YOUR four in his cadence, then land the last line.

verse.text: aghorebhyo 'tha ghorebhyo ghoraghoratarībhyaśca | sarvataḥ śarva sarvebhyo namaste rudrarūpebhyaḥ ||

howto.text: Chant it where Swamiji put it: at the opening of any practice — this is the beginning of the Weekly Sangha. Three to nine rounds, aloud. When to: first thing in the morning, or at any moment of fear — you are addressing the three energies directly. Effect, per the tradition he taught: protection through the eighteen arms and purification of the three channels, body, speech and mind. His own instruction for its spread: 'You should spread this message all over the world.'

verse.text: labdhāṇimādisiddhir vigalitasakalopatāpasantrāsaḥ / tvadbhaktirasāyanapānakriḍhāniṣṭaḥ kadāsīya

howto.text: Anxious about what's coming? Take the verse as a drink-description and sip your current state as rasa.

verse.text: antar apy atitarām aṇīyasī yā tvadaprathanakālikāsti me / tām apīśa parimṛjya sarvataḥ svaṃ svarūpam amalaṃ prakāśaya

howto.text: In self-loathing: rename the stain — it is just the lapse of attention. Wipe = return, not scrub.

verse.text: manasi maline madīyemagnā tvadbhaktimaṇilatā kaṣṭam / na nijān api tanute tānapauruṣeyān svasampadullāsān

howto.text: Say it on the days you feel worst about yourself — the hymn says it for you, better.

verse.text: kharaniṣedhakhadāmṛtapūraṇocchalitadhautavikalpamalasya me / dalitadurjayasaṃśayavairiṇas tvadavalokanam astu nirantaram

howto.text: When the mind feels stained AND doubting: stop scrubbing, start looking — one look inward at the form.

verse.text: vilīne śaṅkaughe sapadi paripūrṇe ca vibhave | saṃhārākhyā mama hṛdi bhidāṃśaṃ praharatu

howto.text: After weeks of inner division — this vs that, me vs it: say it as the surgeon's request, once.

verse.text: śiva ity ekaśabdasya jihvāgre tiṣṭhataḥ sadā / samastaviṣayāsvādo bhakteṣv evāsti ko 'py aho

howto.text: When anything tastes or sounds flat: place Śiva at the tongue's tip and re-taste the next sip or bite.

verse.text: māyāvine viśuddhāya guhyāya prakaṭātmane / sūkṣmāya viśvarūpāya namaś citrāya śambhave

howto.text: When the world turns surreal — say the verse and file the strangeness under citra.

verse.text: ya eṣa vitatasphuradvividhabhāvacakrātmakaḥ parasparavibhedavānviṣayatāmupāgacchati yadekamayabhāvanāvaśata etyabhedānvayaṃ sa śaṃbhuraśivāpaho jayati bodhabhāsāṃ nidhiḥ

howto.text: Use it as the invocation before any prayer-session in this book: name the swirl of your current states as the wheel, then remember the wheel IS the treasury.

verse.text: aho bhaktibharodāracetasāṃ varada tvayi / slāghyaḥ pūjāvidhiḥ ko 'pi yo na yācñākalaṃkitaḥ

howto.text: Notice when you've prayed with a shopping list. Say this verse as the correction, then worship once with nothing attached.

verse.text: śāntakallolaśītācchasvādubhaktisudhāmbudhau / alaukikarasāsvāde susthaiḥ ko 'nāma gaṇyate

howto.text: For peace-practice: dive once, taste once, count nothing — not even the breath.

verse.text: bhavatpūjāmayāsaṅgasambhogasukhino mama / prayātu kālaḥ sakalo 'py ananto 'pīyadarthaye

howto.text: When the day stretches ahead daunting: pray the WHOLE day into the worship-frame, then do the next ordinary thing as its first item.

verse.text: śāntaye na sukhalipsutā manāg bhaktisambhṛtamadeṣu taiḥ prabhoḥ / mokṣamārgaṇaphalāpi nārthanā smaryate hṛdayahāriṇaḥ puraḥ

howto.text: When peace turns into another acquisition-plan — this retreat, that technique, the next course — say it as the disarming.

verse.text: tvatkarṇadeśama dhiśayya mahārghabhāvam ākranditāni mama tucchatarāṇi yānti / vaṃśāntarālapatitāni jalaikadeśakhaṇḍāni mauktikamaṇitvam ivodvahanti

howto.text: When crying or complaining: say it and consciously LAY the noise at his ear — the listener inside.
